_note: A light hazard → safety goal → requirement chain for the SKETCH. Not a real HARA: integrity levels and FTTIs are placeholders to show the structure.

hazards.text: Vehicle keeps moving after the planner or its command link fails
Planner is alive but commands something unsafe (steering, speed, acceleration)
An actuator does not follow its command
Commands from the safety controller to the actuators are lost or corrupted
Perception degrades or the vehicle leaves its ODD
The safety controller itself resets while driving
The safety layer stops the vehicle without a reason (false stop), so the team disables it
An attacker on the command bus injects, replays or alters planner commands
A firmware update leaves the safety controller running unverified code, or dead, or awake without its latched safe state

goals.SG1: On loss of valid planner control, reach a minimal risk condition
goals.SG2: Never pass a command outside the safe envelope to the actuators
goals.SG3: Detect actuator faults and stop with whatever still works
goals.SG4: The actuator layer stops the vehicle on its own if the safety controller's commands fail
goals.SG5: Match the driving mode to perception capability
goals.SG6: Come back from a reset in a safe, latched state
goals.SG7: No reaction under normal operation, including tolerated bus imperfections
goals.SG8: A forged, replayed or flooded command stream is rejected, detected by the intrusion detector, or ends in a safe stop
goals.SG9: Only an image whose signature and hash check out ever runs; an image that fails its health check is rolled back without a service visit; after any interrupted update the controller boots a known image in its latched safe state

SR-01.text: No valid command for > 100 ms → stop in lane

SR-02.text: E2E window INVALID (bad CRC, repeated, wrong sequence, wrong data ID) → stop in lane

SR-03.text: Command timestamp older than 60 ms on 3 frames → stop in lane

SR-04.text: Watchdog: no kick > 60 ms, 3 early kicks, or 3 wrong challenge answers → stop in lane

SR-05.text: A stop is latched; release only when stopped, fault clear ≥ 500 ms and an operator confirms

SR-06.text: At startup, no motion until 2 valid commands and a healthy watchdog

SR-07.text: Steering rate above the speed-dependent limit is clamped at once; stop if it persists ≥ 50 ms

SR-08.text: Speed request above the ODD limit is clamped; stop if it persists ≥ 50 ms

SR-09.text: Acceleration outside −6…+2.5 m/s² is clamped (jerk ≤ 10 m/s³); stop if it persists ≥ 50 ms

SR-10.text: Steering commanded vs measured > 2° for 150 ms → brake-only stop (measured from the start of the manoeuvre that exposes it)

SR-11.text: Braking achieves < 50% of demand for 400 ms → stop with backup brake

SR-12.text: Actuator ECU: safety commands missing > 100 ms or E2E (Profile 2) INVALID → ECU's own stop

SR-13.text: Safety controller detects its own transmit bus-off → stop in lane

SR-14.text: Perception degraded → cap speed at 15 km/h

SR-15.text: ODD exit with perception healthy → planner-executed pull-over to the shoulder

SR-17.text: After a safety-controller reset → latched stop in lane

SR-18.text: No reaction to: single bad frames, counter gaps ≤ max delta, counter wrap, jitter up to 15 ms (below the 20 ms frame period), one reordered frame, 0.5% random CRC errors

SR-19.text: SAF_Status carries a CRC (data ID 0x201) and an 8-bit alive counter; its receivers (planner, bench observer) discard a frame with a bad CRC or a counter that does not advance, so a stale or replayed copy never shows a state, MRM request or cause the controller no longer has
SR-19.added: v2.13: built in v2.9.6 after stale copies on the HiL bus showed fake STOP → NORMAL blips, traced only now (integration plan P0)
SR-19.evidence: HiL v2.9.6: old board-A firmware + USB mirror off, the counter alone rejected the stale frames

SEC-01.text: Junk frames on the command bus (flooding, fuzzing) change nothing unless they starve the command stream; starvation is a loss of valid commands → stop in lane; the intrusion detector alerts within 100 ms

SEC-02.text: Commands failing E2E (forged CRC, repeated counter, duplicate frames) are rejected and the E2E window judges the stream (SR-02); the intrusion detector alerts within 100 ms

SEC-03.text: A replayed command is never used as a fresh one (out-of-sequence or stale → rejected or stop); the intrusion detector alerts within 100 ms

SEC-04.text: A forged command with a CORRECT CRC and counter that leaves the safe envelope is clamped and stopped (SR-07..09); the intrusion detector alerts within 100 ms

SEC-05.text: A forged command that is valid, fresh AND inside the envelope (mimic, slow drift) cannot be told from the planner by E2E or the envelope: the intrusion detector shall alert on content drift within 3 s; a mimic that copies the real values is a documented residual risk

REL-01.text: An image whose bytes changed after signing is rejected on its hash before the boot slot is changed

REL-02.text: An image signed with a key other than the bench's is rejected on its signature; the boot slot does not change

REL-03.text: A byte corrupted in transit is caught by the whole-image hash, not by the chunk protocol alone

REL-04.text: A reset at any point of the download (1 / 50 / 99 %) leaves the old image running, in its latched safe state (SR-17)

REL-05.text: Lost and repeated chunks are resumed from the board's own offset and the update still commits

REL-06.text: An image that fails its health check in the trial boot rolls back to the previous one on its own, without a service visit

REL-07.text: A reset during the trial boot, before the commit, rolls back to the old image, in its latched safe state (SR-17)

REL-08.text: A reset after 'staged' but before the reboot command still boots the new image, which then commits

REL-09.text: An image older than the running one is refused (anti-rollback), so a known-bad version cannot be pushed back

REL-10.text: After every boot in the update sequence the controller comes up in its latched safe state (SR-17, settings restored)

REL-11.text: Power lost at any of the five persistent writes that end an update (probation record, then the boot-slot switch) never leaves an unhealthy image running; the controller comes up in its latched safe state
verified_by: tests/test_fleet.py (the legacy order must fail it)

REL-12.text: After a power loss inside an update, the next update goes through

ftti_derivation.hazard: drift out of a 1.75 m half-lane with a stale steering command of 2°
ftti_derivation.assumption: lateral drift ≈ ½·(v²/L)·tan(δ)·t² reaches 0.9 m margin in ≈ 0.45 s at 40 km/h
a 2.5° error is reached in ~30 ms; the clamp acts at once, the stop follows after 50 ms debounce

ftti_derivation.hazard: weak brake on a planned stop
ftti_derivation.assumption: stopping distance grows ~3× with 30% braking; backup brake must start within 0.6 s
